item.title: Statistics Canada to release October labour force survey numbers today
item.description: OTTAWA — Statistics Canada will release its latest snapshot of the country’s job market today. The agency is set to release its labour force survey for October. The Canadian economy lost 68,000 jobs ...
item.dc:creator: Reuters Staff
item.content:encoded: OTTAWA — Canada’s unemployment rate went up to a six-month high in October and the economy lost a few thousand jobs as the private sector and full-time employment saw declines, data showed on Friday. The unemployment rate edged up to 6.7 per cent in October from 6.5 per cent in the prior month, Statistics Canada said. The last time it was higher than this level was 6.9 per cent jobless rate in April. The economy lost a net of 4,700 jobs in the month, taking the total size of the jobs the economy lost this year to 46,000 overall. The October report highlights a continued weakness in the labour market in Canada that has failed to post any job gains on average this year as trade tensions between the U.S. and Canada worsened and businesses hunkered down to save costs. More than one out of every four person in the employable population of 15 years and older found it difficult to meet its financial needs in terms of transportation, housing, food, clothing and other necessary expenses over the previous four weeks, StatsCan said. On an average monthly basis, the Canadian economy has lost 4,590 jobs this year so far, in contrast to an average gain of 17,606 in 2025, and 33,675 gains in 2024. Analysts polled by Reuters had forecast an increase of 13,600 jobs this month, following a loss of 68,300 jobs in September. They had predicted the unemployment rate to stay unchanged at 6.5 per cent. All the job losses were concentrated in full-time employment which saw jobs shrink by 18,100 last month and almost completely led by a 52,500 jobs in private sector employees. This was the first decline in the private space since February, StatsCan said. Employment in wholesale and retail trade contracted by 28,800 jobs, posting the biggest decline in October, and was followed by transportation and warehousing where employment declined by 10,100 positions. Employment in construction increased by 16,000 in October. The unemployment rate among the youth, or those aged 15 to 24 years, rose 0.7 percentage points to 13.7 per cent last month. This was followed by a rise in jobless rate among people aged 55 and older to 5.5 per cent. Growth in average hourly wages for permanent employees, a closely watched measure of inflation pressures, slowed to two per cent year-on-year in October, from 2.3 per cent in September, Statistics Canada said. (Reporting by Promit Mukherjee; Editing by Dale Smith)

item.title: Black Friday sales are already available as shoppers take advantage of pre-Christmas deals
item.description: It may only be early November, but Black Friday sales offering a variety of shopping discounts are already underway in many stores across Canada.
item.dc:creator: Paul Hollingsworth
item.content:encoded: DARTMOUTH, N.S. - It may only be early November, but Black Friday sales offering a variety of shopping discounts are already underway in many stores across Canada. Black Friday, the day when many retailers across North America offer massive sales to help jump-start the Christmas shopping season, is not until Nov. 27. However, in recent years, there has been an increasing trend to offer cheaper prices and promotions several weeks ahead of the actual day. “Retailers now start their Black Friday sales in the beginning of November,” said retail analyst Bruce Winder. “Best Buy, Canadian Tire, Amazon and a lot of others are out there hammering away every week to offer deals and because of that it has really become Black Friday month now and not just one day.” Winder also pointed out that most shoppers no longer wait until mid-December to begin their holiday shopping. Online and in-store deals have motivated many consumers to purchase products earlier, lengthening the shopping season leading to Dec. 25. “Retailers always want to extend the shopping season and give consumers a reason to log on to a shopping website or to go to the store to buy products,” Winder said. “Retail operators know that shoppers are not going to spend money unless there is a promotion to help them save money at a time when there is an affordability crisis.” Holiday shopping starts early Adrian Fernando, assistant store leader of operations at the Best Buy in Dartmouth, said a lot of customers have flocked to his location and others in the area looking to take advantage of bargains. “Our sales started this past Monday for our early Black Friday promotions, and every week some of those sales will change and then all of the sales will be put back in place during the actual week of Black Friday,” Fernando said. “We get a lot of customers coming in and asking if certain things are on sale and I would say business is going to be double and close to triple the amount that we would usually do, and that includes a lot of online orders.” According to Fernando, there have also been changes in the store’s inventory, with a wider variety of products available for shoppers starting in early November. “This year our hot sellers will be the Bambu Lab 3D printers, and a lot of smartwatches, smartphones and Fitbits,” Fernando said. Winder added that the entire Black Friday concept has become a make-or-break proposition for many companies looking to ramp up pre-Christmas business. “That is why they call it ‘Black Friday,’ because in the past a lot of companies were operating in the red, in other words they were losing money, and then at the end of Black Friday they made so much money that they were in the ‘black’ of making money for the year,” Winder said. “So, depending on the business, this often is a massive must-win month for most retailers.” For shoppers like Jarret Rogers, the early sales are welcomed. “This was regular $100, but I got it for $45,” he said referring to his new headphones. “I really didn’t need this, and I didn’t need to buy anything, but I went into a store because I saw the sales, so I decided to buy it.”

item.title: 6 biotech stocks for a volatile bull market: Jon Erlichman
item.description: Legend makes a cancer treatment with Johnson & Johnson that turns a patient’s own immune cells into cancer fighters. Sales are rising, and about 70 per cent of analysts rate the stock a buy. Rahim ...
item.content:encoded:
Biotech stocks can be volatile, even in a bull market. So how do investors avoid the traps? We asked Eden Rahim of Next Edge Capital, who has had plenty of success investing in biotech. He estimates roughly 40 of the companies he’s invested in over the years have been acquired, including three companies he highlighted on Ticker Take last year.

His game plan is to own companies that are far along in drug development, where the biggest risks are behind them. Rahim says the current bull market has cooled for two reasons. Rising interest rates are tough on biotech, since many of these companies won’t make a profit for years. In addition, Moderna shot up on cancer vaccine news, and funds that were betting against it had to sell other biotech stocks to cover their short positions. None of this worries him, though. He told us on the latest episode of Ticker Take that it creates new opportunities in several stocks, which we’ve outlined below. Rahim says he owns or has owned most of them. As always, this is not financial advice. Cytokinetics (CYTK) Cytokinetics makes a heart drug for a condition where the heart muscle squeezes too hard and can’t pump enough blood, especially during exercise. More than 90 per cent of analysts rate the stock a buy. Rahim says the fact that Novartis was once reportedly interested in buying the company suggests its current valuation is more than fair. Legend Biotech (LEGN) Legend makes a cancer treatment with Johnson & Johnson that turns a patient’s own immune cells into cancer fighters. Sales are rising, and about 70 per cent of analysts rate the stock a buy. Rahim says the market is worried about new competition, but he sees that as an opportunity and good value for investors. TG Therapeutics (TGTX) TG makes a multiple sclerosis drug that is taking market share from Roche. More than 85 per cent of analysts rate it as a buy. Revenue has roughly doubled each year for three years, and Rahim says a new version of the treatment that patients can take at home could widen its reach. Alpha Cognition (ACOG) Alpha is a small Canadian company with a new Alzheimer’s drug. Only a few analysts cover it, but all of them like it. The drug is an improved version of an older one with fewer side effects. Rahim expects sales to keep growing over the next year. ClearPoint Neuro (CLPT) ClearPoint makes a device that guides treatments deep into the brain. Like Alpha Cognition, it has limited analyst coverage, but the analysts who track it like it. Rahim says dozens of partners are testing brain treatments for conditions like Huntington’s and Parkinson’s, and any that get approved could mean more business for ClearPoint. Nektar Therapeutics (NKTR) Nektar is developing a new eczema treatment, a condition that causes itchy, inflamed skin. The rival to beat is Dupixent, the standard drug for eczema. Rahim told us many patients don’t respond to Dupixent, and Nektar’s drug works differently, by using an immune cell that calms inflammation. It is also being tested for a type of hair loss, where the standard treatment carries a serious safety warning. More than 70 per cent of the analysts who track Nektar rate it a buy. The Ticker Take Rahim estimates big drug companies are about to lose patent protection on more than $100 billion in revenue by 2030. In his opinion, they’ll need new drugs to replace what they’re losing, and buying a biotech company is one way to fill the pipeline. While the stocks he’s highlighted can be volatile, he sees all of them offering opportunities that big pharma may eventually notice too. Jon Erlichman is a BNN Bloomberg contributor and the host of Ticker Take on YouTube . item.title: Gold investors are buying into declining prices: Brooke Thackray
item.description: The price of gold has declined 25 per cent since hitting its all-time-high of US$5,417 on Jan. 28, 2026. In the background, there has been increasing buying support from central banks, institutions ...
item.content:encoded:
The price of gold has declined 25 per cent since hitting its all-time-high of US$5,417 on Jan. 28, 2026. In the background, there has been increasing buying support from central banks, institutions and retail investors. Although the price of gold has not substantially recovered from its October low, gold is poised to move higher in the not-so-distant future.

Central banks have been net purchasers of gold since 2010 and have sharply increased their purchases since 2022, increasing their net purchases to over 800 tonnes yearly. Purchases in 2026 are set to once again come in at over 800 tonnes, with year-to-date purchases through the third quarter registering over 600 tonnes. Brooke Thackray The People’s Bank of China (PBoC) has been a huge buyer of gold and has been a net buyer for the last 23 months. What is interesting is that the PBoC has been increasing its official purchases sharply as gold has fallen in price since January 2026. In the graph below, the purple bars (PBoC net purchases) have been rising every month since gold started its decline in January 2026. Brooke Thackray It’s not just central banks that have been increasing their purchases, but also retail and institutional investors. In the graph below, the blue shaded line represents the total known ETF holdings of gold. This is essentially the sum of all gold troy ounces held in all gold ETFs in the world. The number of ounces held in ETFs is independent of the price of gold. The gold ounces held in gold ETFs shows a decline from 2020 to mid-2024 (section 1 of graph) as the gold price (gold line) was generally consolidating a bit below to a bit above $2,000. In this time period, investors lost interest in gold as it was moving sideways at the same time the North American stock markets were moving higher, providing a better investment alternative. Brooke Thackray In section 2 of the graph, from mid-2023 to early 2026, investors were increasing their buying of gold ETFs as the price of gold was increasing. In section 3 of the graph, from early 2026 to mid-2026 investors once again became net sellers, as the price of gold declined. Section 4 of the graph is different compared to the previous sections. It shows that investors have been net buyers of gold, even as the price of gold has been declining. This has happened before but is not the typical behaviour for investors. Typically, investors are net sellers of gold ETFs when gold is declining. The price of gold is set in many markets with different buyers. With central banks continuing to be net buyers of gold and retail and institutional investors showing increasing interest in buying gold, this is building a good foundation for gold to move higher. Increased buying from these groups does not ensure that gold will move higher in price, but it is setting the conditions for gold to perform well when other variables turn favourable. For example, if the U.S. dollar or interest rates decline this could be the catalyst for further buying to push the price of gold higher.
